messages.subject: geom_sf() tibble linked issue
parts:
Hi guys,

I have an issue when using the geom_sf() with spatial layers. ggplot2 is not plotting maps using sf objects read from shape files (here in the example downloaded from https://gadm.org/download_country_v3.html).
The R console retruns an error which I believe is linked with how tibble are handled in ggplot2. It was perfectly working before. Any helps are really appreciated.

Thanks!

Antonello

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

mapAus1 <- st_read(dsn="D:/", layer="gadm36_AUS_0")
mapAus2 <- readRDS(file="D:/gadm36_AUS_0_sf.rds")
plotMap <- ggplot() +
           geom_sf(data=mapAus2, colour=NA, fill="grey74") +
           coord_sf(datum=NA) +
           theme_classic()

> plotMap
```

messages.subject: Re: geom_sf() tibble linked issue
parts:
I think your issue (at least in the code you've shared) is that you
probably have saved something in the rds file that isn't an sf object.
The following works fine for me:

library(sf)
library(ggplot2)


file_loc <- file.path(tempdir(),"aus_tmp.rds")
download.file(url =
"https://biogeo.ucdavis.edu/data/gadm3.6/Rsf/gadm36_AUS_0_sf.rds",
destfile = file_loc)

mapAus2 <- readRDS(file_loc)

plotMap <- ggplot() +
geom_sf(data=mapAus2, colour=NA, fill="grey74") +
coord_sf(datum=NA) +
theme_classic()

plotMap

## Another way to do this is the use `getData` from the {raster} package:
mapAus2 <- raster::getData(country = 'AUS', level = 0)

plotMap <- ggplot() +
geom_sf(data=mapAus2, colour=NA, fill="grey74") +
coord_sf(datum=NA) +
theme_classic()

plotMap

thanks for the reply.

Unfortunately, using your code the error persist...it is not a problem of the sf object (UC Davis and GADM use the same .rds), the error is recreated using the shapefile and also with the ratser getData function.
Which verision of tibble have you installed? I believe this is a problem with the github dev version of tibble (installed in my R).
https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3453

Cheers,

Antonello

Great - seems like you've fixed the issue then. Just revert back to
the CRAN version of tibble? Just a note: the rds file is not the
shapefile and just the exported R object. A shapefile is a proprietary
format that includes at least 3 files. Obviously those are also
available via the links you sent.

Sam
